userStories.title: SQLite store and migrations
userStories.description: bb-store with rusqlite (bundled), WAL mode, forward-only migrations. Tables for calls (provider, model, tokens, latency, status, trace/span ids) and settings. Content capture column nullable, gated by a setting that defaults to off. Model recording as an append-only event log: events(run_id, seq, kind, ts, payload_ref) with seq strictly increasing per run; calls is a projection derived from events (CQRS). When content capture is on, store each message once in a content-addressed blobs table keyed by SHA-256, since agents resend the whole history every call. Hash-chain the event log from day one: each event stores prev_hash and event_hash = SHA-256 over its canonical bytes (RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization) plus prev_hash. Retrofitting this later would break every existing log.
acceptanceCriteria: Migrations run idempotently on startup
WAL enabled (tested)
capture_content setting defaults to false
events table is insert-only (no UPDATE/DELETE paths in code; tested)
seq is gap-free and monotonic per run under concurrent writes
Identical message content across calls is stored once (tested)
Editing or deleting any stored event is detected by a verify function (tested)
references: /mnt/project system-design-101 database-and-storage: event sourcing ('designed with determinism')
system-design-101 how-it-works: exchange sequences orders so replay is deterministic
https://cstack.github.io/db_tutorial/ (optional background only; SQLite is used, not rebuilt)

userStories.title: Plan M5: Delegation + task board (ACP host)
userStories.description: ACP client host: start sessions on any adapter (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, API-only models), stream updates, own fs/* and terminal/* with recording. Task board with dependencies and acceptance criteria. Approvals from session/request_permission shown in the UI. Every worker session is ephemeral: fresh session per task, closed and released when the task ends. Worker registry and identity: lifecycle states requested -> cast -> hired -> active -> wrapping -> released, plus revoked and expired (orphans reaped on restart). Three identities: (1) spec digest = SHA-256 over the canonical worker spec (adapter+version, model, soul digest, tools/permissions, policy digest), same config -> same digest; (2) instance id = UUIDv7 plus an ephemeral Ed25519 key minted at hire and held only by the daemon, never by the worker process; (3) the install root key signs a hire record binding instance key, spec digest, task, budget and expiry. At wrap, emit an in-toto Statement v1 (DSSE-signed by the instance key) whose subjects are the produced artifacts and whose predicate holds spec digest, sides digest, soul digest, usage and checkpoint reference, then destroy the instance key. Sub-agents spawned by a worker get narrower capabilities than their parent, never wider. Record the model version the provider actually returned, since a model name can change behind the same spec.
